events.title: UK Retail Sales Rebound Amid Be Ready Campaign
events.description: UK retail sales rebounded strongly in October as consumers stocked up on long-life food items following the government's Be Ready campaign launch, data from the Office for National Statistics showed Friday. Retail sales increased 0.7 percent in October from September, when the volume was down 0.6 percent. Economists had forecast sales to remain flat.

events.title: P&G Plans To Cut Up To 30% Product Supply Jobs By 2030; Confirms FY27 Outlook
events.description: Consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble Co. or P&G announced its plans for a ?20 percent to 30 percent reduction in product supply workforce, including contractors, by 2030. The firm targets up to $10 billion in productivity savings from ?fiscal years 2027-2030. The move is part of its productivity restructuring efforts amid the increasing pressure on supply-chain costs.

events.title: European Shares Set To Drift Lower As AI Selloff Deepens
events.description: European stocks look set to open lower on Friday as AI trade doubts continue to weigh on global technology shares.

events.title: Indian Shares Off Day's Lows As IT Stocks Surge
events.description: Indian shares opened lower on Friday as a global AI selloff on concerns over slower AI infrastructure spending and expectations of prolonged monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve rattled investors.

events.title: Australian Market Extends Early Losses In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian stock market is extending its early losses in mid-market moves on Friday, adding to the losses in the previous six sessions, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is falling to near the 8,600 level, with weakness across most sectors led by gold miners and technology stocks.

events.title: Asian Markets A Sea Of Red Amid Tech Sell-off
events.description: Asian stock markets are a sea of red on Friday, following the broadly negative cues on Wall Street overnight, dragged by markets in Taiwan, South Korea and Japan amid a sell-off in semiconductor and technology stocks on lingering concerns about where the AI trade goes from here. Commodity-related stocks also took a hit. Concerns of re-escalation in the Middle East also gripped the markets.

events.title: Indian Shares Seen Lower As AI Selloff Deepens
events.description: Indian shares are seen opening lower on Friday due to a sharp sell-off in global equities.

events.title: Thai Stock Market May See Renewed Selling Pressure On Friday
events.description: The Thai stock market on Thursday ended the three-day slide in which it had given up almost 35 points or 2.2 percent. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just above the 1,470-point plateau although it may turn lower again on Friday.

events.title: Japanese Market Sharply Lower; Plunging 3.7%
events.description: The Japanese market is trading sharply lower on Friday, reversing the gains in the previous two sessions, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is tumbling 3.7 percent to below the 57,250 level, with weakness across most sectors led by index heavyweights and technology stocks.

events.title: Indonesia Stock Market Tipped To Open In The Red
events.description: The Indonesia stock market has finished lower in four straight sessions, retreating more than 125 points or 2.2 percent along the way. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just beneath the 5,200-point plateau and it's looking at another soft start again on Friday.

events.title: Lower Open Predicted For Hong Kong Stock Market
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has finished lower in three straight sessions, sinking more than 900 points or 4 percent along the way. The Hang Seng now sits just beneath the 22,850-point plateau and it figures to see continued consolidation again on Friday.

events.title: Australian Market Significantly Lower
events.description: The Australian stock market is trading significantly lower on Friday, extending the losses in the previous six sessions, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is falling to near the 8,650 level, with weakness across most sectors led by gold miners and technology stocks.

events.title: China Stock Market Tipped To Open Under Water On Friday
events.description: The China stock market turned lower again on Thursday, one day after ending the four-day losing streak in which it had slumped almost 100 points or 2.7 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,580-point plateau and the losses may accelerate on Friday.
